sections.title: Social Inequality and Health: Global Implications
sections.description: How are health, illness, and treatment shaped by society and its structures? This course provides an overview of how various social determinants of health—e.g., race, class, gender, culture, and environment—are connected to health disparities and shape access to healthcare. Specifically, we examine how an uneven distribution of resources and contested power dynamics among social groups lead to persistent inequalities in health outcomes in both the U.S. and global contexts. Additionally, we explore the professionalization of medicine, the industrialization of healthcare, as well as the forces that have led to “medicalization” in our society. Finally, we will examine the political economy of health care—that is, how governments interact with markets to influence medical services and what health care reform might look like.
